title: LETTER 7: Letter to Editor — Digital Rupee (CBDC) and Its Benefits

blocks.content: Topic: Write a letter to the editor of a financial newspaper appreciating the launch of India's Central Bank Digital Currency (Digital Rupee) and its potential to transform the economy.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Digital Rupee (e₹) is a Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) issued by the Reserve Bank of India as official sovereign currency in digital form.
CBDC significantly reduces operational expenditures related to printing, distributing, and managing physical currency.
It facilitates instant, peer-to-peer real-time finality in settlement without requiring commercial bank intermediaries.
The Digital Rupee enhances financial inclusion, promotes innovation in digital payments, and secures public trust in sovereign money.

blocks.content: The Digital Rupee represents a landmark transformation in India's monetary architecture, combining the sovereign trust of cash with the speed and safety of digital technology.
Subject: India's Digital Rupee — A Transformative Step Towards a Modern Economy

rows: Digital form of sovereign fiat currency
Payment overlay interface for bank accounts
Can be held in a digital wallet independently
Mandatorily linked to an active bank account

blocks.content: I write to commend the Reserve Bank of India for the successful pilot launch of the Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC), popularly known as the Digital Rupee or e-Rupee, which commenced its retail phase in December 2022. This landmark initiative places India among a select group of nations exploring sovereign digital currencies, alongside China's digital yuan and the European Central Bank's digital euro.

The Digital Rupee holds immense promise for India's financial ecosystem. First, being issued and backed by the RBI, it carries zero default risk — unlike commercial bank deposits which are insured only up to Rs. 5 lakh per depositor under the DICGC scheme. Second, it can dramatically reduce the enormous cost of printing, storing, and distributing physical currency — estimated at over Rs. 4,000 crore annually by various studies. Third, for cross-border remittances, a bilateral CBDC link (such as India's UPI–Singapore's PayNow linkage) can reduce transaction costs from the current 6–7% to near zero, benefiting millions of overseas Indian workers. Fourth, programmable CBDC can enable targeted government benefit transfers, ensuring that subsidies are used only for specified purposes — reducing leakage and misuse.

However, challenges remain. Privacy concerns around state surveillance of financial transactions must be addressed through robust legal safeguards. Cybersecurity infrastructure must be fortified to prevent digital theft. Public trust must be built gradually through transparent communication.

The Digital Rupee is not merely a technology upgrade — it is the foundation of India's future digital economy. Your newspaper's continued coverage of this subject will inform and educate the public on this crucial development.

items: CBDC is sovereign legal tender issued directly by the RBI, distinguishing it entirely from decentralized private cryptocurrencies.
RBI launched CBDC in two distinct phases: e₹-W (Wholesale for interbank settlements) and e₹-R (Retail for general public use).
Examiners frequently contrast CBDC (which is the actual currency) with UPI (which is merely a payment routing platform).

blocks.content: Examiner's Tip: When writing on contemporary banking topics (CBDC, UPI, Digital Lending), show depth by mentioning specific details — Rs.4,000 crore printing costs, DICGC limit, bilateral links. This immediately differentiates a bank professional's essay from a general one.
